summary.text: A 57-year-old woman with schizoaffective disorder developed hallucinations, delusions, agitation, echolalia and disorganized behavior after gastrectomy for a gastrointestinal stromal tumor, then fever 40 °C, diaphoresis, rigidity and CK elevation that raised suspicion of NMS.

Antipsychotics were stopped and she received IV fluids, IV dantrolene and oral lorazepam; CK fell but catatonic and autonomic features persisted. After transfer she was re-diagnosed with malignant catatonia (admission BP 175/110 mmHg, HR 127 bpm, BT 38.4 °C); CT and blood tests were unrevealing.

IV lorazepam 6 mg started Day 1; ECT transfer was not possible; oral guanfacine 2 mg was started Day 7 with rapid motor improvement, then adjusted to 3 and 4 mg with lorazepam taper, olanzapine titration to 7.5 mg and later quetiapine 25 mg.

EEG on Day 10 was within normal limits and excluded delirium and epilepsy; Day 45 EEG normal. Mild hypotension and dizziness occurred Days 24-35 with lorazepam reductions. She was discharged on Day 54 in remission on guanfacine 4 mg, olanzapine 7.5 mg and quetiapine 25 mg and has lived a normal daily life with her family.

summary.text: A 54-year-old woman without prior psychiatric history was admitted with schizophrenia (hallucinations and delusions); whole-body CT, EEG and blood tests excluded organic causes. She received risperidone 4 mg with olanzapine 10 mg, then risperidone was replaced by paliperidone LAI 150 mg every four weeks, with an additional 100 mg dose one week later, and she was discharged home.

After the second paliperidone 150 mg dose and olanzapine discontinuation, about two weeks later she developed whispering, grimacing, muscle rigidity and mutism meeting DSM-5-TR catatonia criteria; lorazepam 3 mg gave partial benefit, paliperidone LAI was stopped and biperiden was ineffective.

Guanfacine 2 mg was added when she could not eat solid food; rigidity and grimacing resolved over a few weeks, lorazepam and biperiden were tapered off, olanzapine was restarted at 2.5 mg (reduced to 1.25 mg for drowsiness) and guanfacine was reduced to 1 mg for dizziness and fatigue. Remission was maintained and she lives a normal daily life at home.

summary.text: A 56-year-old man with schizophrenia, stable on paliperidone LAI 150 mg every four weeks, received the scheduled injection while hospitalized for COVID-19. Several days later, shortly after recovering, he developed mutism, muscular rigidity and severe motor impairment needing a urinary catheter; trihexyphenidyl and ethyl loflazepate did not help.

On admission he had grimacing, muscle rigidity and mutism meeting DSM-5-TR catatonia criteria; head CT, chest radiography, ECG and blood tests excluding endocrine crisis and infection were unrevealing.

Guanfacine 2 mg (chosen over increasing benzodiazepines) improved limb movement, resolved mutism and allowed catheter removal within days; it was raised to 3 mg, paliperidone LAI reduced to 100 mg and other agents tapered. Mild hypotension and bradycardia led to guanfacine 1 mg, vital signs normalized, remission was maintained and he was discharged home.

summary.text: A 62-year-old man with schizophrenia (three prior hospitalizations; on risperidone 7 mg and levomepromazine 10 mg) was admitted with worsening persecutory delusions toward his cohabiting father and explosive agitation; admission laboratory evaluation was within normal limits. Risperidone and intramuscular olanzapine were ineffective.

He then developed manic symptoms and received lithium carbonate 400 mg, followed by stupor, muscular rigidity and mutism and a diagnosis of catatonia. Lithium was stopped; lorazepam (IV 2 mg then oral 3 mg daily) resolved the stupor but not the agitation.

Guanfacine 2 mg was started and titrated up to 6 mg; agitation and hallucinatory-delusional states improved and lorazepam was stopped. Risperidone was replaced by brexpiprazole 2 mg. Mild hypotension and bradycardia led to guanfacine 4 mg, vital signs normalized, remission was maintained and he was discharged home.

summary.text: A 63-year-old man with schizoaffective disorder was admitted for a depressive state (decreased motivation, fatigue) on risperidone LAI 25 mg/2 weeks, levomepromazine, valproate, carbamazepine, sertraline and long-term etizolam, nitrazepam and triazolam. Because of repeated falls, including one with major temporal artery bleeding, the benzodiazepines were tapered and discontinued.

He then developed mutism, negativism, mannerisms, stereotypy, agitation, grimacing and echolalia and was diagnosed with catatonia; benzodiazepine withdrawal was considered a likely contributing factor. Risperidone LAI, levomepromazine and sertraline were stopped and brexpiprazole 1 mg was started without benefit; intramuscular diazepam 5 mg gave partial relief.

Oral guanfacine 2 mg and lorazepam 3 mg gradually improved symptoms; lorazepam was reduced to 0.5 mg for postural instability while guanfacine was raised to 3 mg, and carbamazepine was replaced by quetiapine 100 mg for suspected hyponatremia (sodium 128 mEq/L) and drug-induced SIADH. Remission was maintained on brexpiprazole 2 mg, quetiapine, guanfacine and lorazepam, and he was discharged home.

summary.text: A 53-year-old woman with treatment-resistant schizophrenia on long-term risperidone 12 mg, quetiapine 400 mg and lorazepam 3 mg had persistent catatonia with prolonged stupor, negativism and mutism requiring nasogastric feeding.

Adding guanfacine 2 mg let her communicate verbally, but she reported her mind felt scrambled, her hallucinations and delusions became pronounced and guanfacine was stopped at her request. Clozapine later produced remission at 200 mg daily.
